summary: A member's mail readers start reading its messages shard: the recipient page (/v1/messages/page?to=) and a single message read include stream items, and a stream item's staged, delivered, read and closed are recorded on the member with an offset receipt instead of a graph claim. The filtered and unpaged message lists, waits and the mailbox stream still read the graph only and follow in the next change

replay.detail: No graph claim, projection or cache changes. The shard gains two derived tables, filled from its own claims when they are created.

schema.detail: The messages shard (shards/messages/claims.sqlite3) gains stream_messages, an index of its message.sent items by recipient, kept by a trigger, and stream_lifecycle, this member's local lifecycle record per message. The graph database and its storage version are unchanged.

rules.detail: Nothing writes message.sent to the shard yet, so on a real fleet every page and read is what it was. A stream item's lifecycle follows the graph's message transitions (an agent's read follows its delivery; a person's read, a custody read, the runtime's withdrawal and a delegated close may skip steps), a replayed or earlier step settles to what is recorded, and it is never replicated.

compatibility.detail: POST /v1/messages/{id}/claims and mailbox receipts answer a stream item with a claim-shaped record whose id starts offset-receipt/; the record shape is unchanged. A mailbox receipt for a stream item is checked against the same mailbox fence as a graph receipt. A lifecycle post for a stream item with expected_subject set is refused with expected-subject-unsupported; no built-in caller sets it. A delegated or successor transition on a stream item is refused with stream-lifecycle-unsupported until the graph write rules cover stream items. A stream item's created_index is offset past 2^48 so it sorts after every graph index. No client-v0 field is added or removed.

downtime.detail: Creating the two tables on an empty shard is immediate.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to the previous release is safe: earlier builds ignore the shard and its new tables, and no graph claim was written. A stream item's local lifecycle stays in the shard and is read again after the next upgrade. fleet::previous_release_mail_reads_beside_stream_items_across_upgrade_and_rollback runs this path against the previous release.
